What do the UV maps look like?

Primitive meshes UV each side individually with spacing between each cube, could be that blender tries to keep seams together resulting in less pixels wasted to create spacing and thus more resolution for each face.

> What do the UV maps look like?

Using Godot's **View UV2** function in the Mesh menu at the top of the 3D editor viewport (note that aspect ratio isn't preserved):

Primitive BoxMesh | Single Blender cube from *Multiple Imported Scenes* example | Single imported scene[^1]
-|-|-
![Primitive BoxMesh](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b988a034-5e9e-49ab-b2ac-d335ec771e15) | ![Single Blender cube](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/54864ac1-14a1-4f53-a8b6-36712fcd2e5b) | ![Single imported scene](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e49055ef-4d2a-40db-884f-9bff34bc4928)

[^1]: This contains UVs from all cubes in that scene, including the larger ground mesh.

Comparison between Godot and Blender UV2 (with Godot's layout rotated by 90 degrees in GIMP for easier comparison):

![UV2 Comparison animation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/da5ae0e8-47ef-4463-a4f2-2d7199cce4e7)

Notice the lines missing at the top/sides for Godot; it's due to the UV2 preview in the editor being cropped. While this is a bug in the UV2 preview, it highlights the lack of padding around the edges of the UV layout (along with the reduced padding between faces).

@Calinou if I remember correctly we indeed don't have padding on the upper and left edge of the texture.
It would be fairly straight forward to change that.

@Calinou I'm just theorising but I don't think the problem is the padding size, it's that we don't have padding on the left and top edges for the texture. So I think we need to add an offset to all UVs of half the size of the padding to 'center' the UV map on the texture.

> I'm just theorising but I don't think the problem is the padding size, it's that we don't have padding on the left and top edges for the texture.

I added padding to the top and left edges, as demonstrated by the top/left lines now being visible in the UV2 preview (they are no longer clipped by its `clip_contents` property).

> I added padding to the top and left edges, as demonstrated by the top/left lines now being visible in the UV2 preview (they are no longer clipped by its `clip_contents` property).

Ah, then I misread your code because I didn't see the offset  being introduced,
But it still doesn't resolve the issue? I don't know what the difference is then between the imported meshes and the generated meshes. Very strange.

Its looking like the UV generator doesn't snap vertexes to texel's correctly, this also causes light leaks, and can also cause seams to bleed on to other parts of the lightmap with certain combinations of lightmap scale from model and bake panels

> Its looking like the UV generator doesn't snap vertexes to texel's correctly, this also causes light leaks, and can also cause seams to bleed on to other parts of the lightmap with certain combinations of lightmap scale from model and bake panels

In this case, shouldn't the lightmapper perform the snapping?

> > Its looking like the UV generator doesn't snap vertexes to texel's correctly, this also causes light leaks, and can also cause seams to bleed on to other parts of the lightmap with certain combinations of lightmap scale from model and bake panels
> 
> In this case, shouldn't the lightmapper perform the snapping?

Yes sorry, I should have said "the lightmapper UV generator".

There used to be an issue like this with Blender lightmap unwraps, if the UV vertexes weren't snapped correctly obvious seams would appear when viewing mipmaps, and if the gaps between areas were too small the extended edges could bleed on to each other. Similar to this case, it was an arbitrary floating point value to set the gaps when using the lightmap unwrapper, and the artist would have to manually calculate the correct fraction based on the texture canvas size.

I've discovered so far, with very careful massaging of the model import texel size, manual adjustment of lightmap size hint values (after making unique) and selection of lightmap scale value in the lightmapGI node. seams and leaks can nearly be completely eliminated. However its a battle that cannot be won due to lack of resolution in the input fields, and the time cost in repeated guesswork. Maybe the model import value should be a fraction, and the GI tweaks value a "texels per metre", or vice versa?

The gaps and generated seams blending should probably be based on number of mipmaps generated, eg panel gaps of 9 pixels and seams of 4 for 3 levels.

As for the mystery light leaks, they can occur even when using blockers on the back of a polymesh wall unless the values are tweaked just right. I'm unsure if it should be snapped to texel centre or corner just yet. My current working theory is that; if a texel for a panel when rendering lightmaps, counts as being part of the panel, but its worldspace coordinate lands *just* outside the UV, its still traced, but it completely misses adjacent floors or walls etc. (This also occurs when only baking sky light, indicating its not just an issue with precision when tracing to the sun)

Its either that or the seam blending generator has an issue where its picking up light from the wrong places. (or a bit of both at the same time)


Hope that helps tracking it down, hit me up with links to other issues related, or let me know if you'd like an MRP

Just as a note for additional future features. It might be handy for an object that's set to static light, but that does not have a UV2 lightmap unwrap, to still block light paths. That way an asset artist can generate a "hull" for blocking light (in my case I used Blenders Solidify modifier, but then there is wasted lightmap texture for the internal areas), or manually place light blockers for certain effects, or allow back faces to also block light when baking GI. With the new "shadow maps off" selection, having a static but not unwrapped object still block light, gives artists control over all aspects of what casts shadows independent of whether it has light mapping
🤔 💭

Wrote up with screen shots what I've found in a separate post, so the team can merge/reference where needed.

Its looking like vertex winding order is miss-matched between the UV map and the lightmap edge bleed generator

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/100397

> [@Calinou](https://github.com/Calinou) I'm just theorising but I don't think the problem is the padding size, it's that we don't have padding on the left and top edges for the texture. So I think we need to add an offset to all UVs of half the size of the padding to 'center' the UV map on the texture.

I thought the same thing at first, followed by wondering if it was texel centre/edge alignment.
It's looking like it *might* be getting the wrong edge data based on winding order, but I'm not familiar enough with the code to find and test it. Either way, hopefully seeing it under the conditions of rotating the UV's helps the team nail it down 🎉  See above link

Thanks for the detailed reply 🙂

See https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/96538.

found a script workaround for this. instead of building your scene out of mesh primitives build it with CSG. then use `bake_static_mesh()` to turn it into a single `ArrayMesh` and `lightmap_unwrap()` the generated mesh to prepare for baking. the only downside is you need to run the tool script every time you modify level geometry.
